title: How to challenge a friend to the Daily quiz
practice: Play today’s main challenge, then invite a friend to beat your score.

sections.html:
Finish today’s main Daily, choose “Challenge a friend”, then share the invitation link. Your friend gets the same main challenge and your score to beat. No account is needed to play.

You could quietly admire your result. Or you could appoint yourself Unofficial Champion of the Group Chat and give someone a chance to object.

The Daily quiz changes each day, so send the challenge while today’s round is still available.
sections.title: A small score. A very grand title.

sections.html:
Finish the main Daily, then choose Challenge a friend. The invitation includes your main-game points and a link. You can edit the message before copying it into your own chat, or use the share option when your device offers it.

Keep the link and score; add a line you would actually send. Something like:

Your turn, Sam. I’m claiming the sofa champion title until you beat this.

Or, for a friend who prefers lower stakes: “Fancy trying this? I want to know which bit catches you out.” A private joke beats a formal announcement every time.
sections.title: Make the invitation sound like you

sections.html:
A screenshot of the questions is a generous gift to your opponent. So is “be careful with the one about planets”. Even a tiny hint changes the challenge.

Share the invitation or your score, and save the explanation for afterwards. The fun conversation starts when you can both say which answer seemed obvious—and which one absolutely was not.

For a fair comparison, use your main-game points. Optional extras can change the full Daily total, so comparing that against someone who played only the main game would be apples versus apples plus a bonus banana.
sections.title: Which score should you compare?

sections.html:
Your friend can play without an account. Try it on the same day: the Daily changes at 00:00 UTC, and an old invitation leads to the current challenge.

Compare scores in your chat when you have both finished. A draw can stay a draw. The prize can be choosing the next film, naming the group chat for an hour, or simply a deeply unnecessary victory emoji.

If your friend does not fancy it today, leave the invitation there. A good challenge feels like an invitation, not a task.
